summary:
Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map

Exploring Mars presents unique challenges, especially when navigating unfamiliar terrain and identifying suitable paths across its surface. Our project, Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map, is an interactive web-based application focused on Jezero Crater, designed to make Martian exploration easier and more accessible.

We developed a mapping platform that allows users to explore the Martian surface, inspect geographic coordinates, switch between available map layers, plan routes between selected locations, and calculate distances. By bringing these features together in one interface, the project provides a practical way to visualize locations and explore possible paths across the Martian landscape.

Our solution addresses the challenge of navigating and understanding an unfamiliar planetary environment through accessible mapping technology and interactive exploration tools. It demonstrates how digital mapping and route-planning concepts can contribute to future planetary exploration.

This project is important because understanding terrain and planning movement are essential considerations for exploring other planets. Our goal is to make Martian geographic information easier to interact with while encouraging innovation in space exploration through technology.
details:
AbdulRahman:

Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map

1. What Does the Project Do?

Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map is an interactive web-based application focused on exploring Jezero Crater on Mars. It aims to make Martian exploration more accessible by providing users with a digital map that brings together useful navigation and exploration features.

The application allows users to explore the Martian surface, inspect geographic coordinates, switch between available map layers, select locations, plan routes between different points, and calculate the distances between them.

2. How Does It Work?

The project uses an interactive mapping interface that allows users to navigate and explore the selected Martian region.

Users can interact with the map to:

• Explore different locations across the Martian surface.
• Select locations and view their geographic coordinates.
• Switch between available map layers to explore different visual representations.
• Plan routes between selected points.
• Calculate distances between locations to understand the length of a planned journey.

By combining these functions in one interface, the application provides a straightforward way to interact with Martian geographic information.

3. Benefits and Intended Impact

The project aims to:

• Make exploring Martian geography easier and more interactive.
• Improve accessibility to geographic information about Mars.
• Demonstrate how digital mapping can support planetary exploration.
• Help users visualize possible routes and understand distances between locations.
• Encourage interest in space science, planetary research, and future human exploration.

Its intended long-term impact is to demonstrate how accessible technology can contribute to planning and understanding exploration beyond Earth.

4. Tools, Programming Languages, and Technologies

Our team used the following technologies:

• HTML: To structure the website and its content.
• CSS: To design the interface and organize the visual layout.
• JavaScript: To implement interactive mapping features, coordinate inspection, map-layer controls, route planning, and distance calculations.
• GitHub: To store the source code, manage project files, and collaborate as a team.
• ChatGPT and Claude: To assist with development, programming explanations, problem-solving, and debugging.

The project is a software-based web application and does not require specialized hardware for its current implementation.

5. What Makes the Project Creative and Innovative?

The creativity of our project comes from combining multiple exploration and navigation functions into one accessible Martian mapping experience.

Rather than presenting geographic information as static content, we developed an interactive platform where users can explore locations, switch between map layers, inspect coordinates, and plan journeys.

Applying familiar web-mapping concepts to the exploration of another planet creates an engaging way to understand planetary environments and demonstrates how existing digital technologies can be adapted for space exploration.

6. Factors Considered by the Team

During development, our team considered several important factors:

• Accessibility: Making the website straightforward and easy to navigate.
• Usability: Keeping the mapping interface organized and understandable.
• Navigation: Allowing users to select locations and explore possible routes.
• Distance Awareness: Providing distance calculations to help users understand the scale of journeys.
• Information Presentation: Organizing available map layers and coordinates clearly.
• Technical Feasibility: Choosing web technologies that our team could develop, test, and maintain.
• Collaboration: Dividing responsibilities between team members and integrating their contributions into one project.
• Scientific Accuracy: Recognizing the importance of reliable planetary information and avoiding unsupported claims about terrain conditions or navigation safety.

7. Overall Goal

AbdulRahman:

Our ultimate goal is to create an accessible interactive tool that demonstrates how technology, mapping, and creative problem-solving can support the exploration of Mars. We hope our project inspires further development of digital tools that make planetary exploration easier to understand and more engaging.
